What’s Happening
Starting on 3/17, we will be working with DTI to reduce the number of Windows accounts with Local Administrator access as part of a statewide effort to strengthen and protect our systems. This effort ensures our compliance with IRS requirements.  Thank you for your cooperation and support as we work to keep our technology secure.
________________________________________
Why This is Happening
Reducing Local Administrator rights is a necessary security best practice that helps protect State systems by:
•	Protecting the State Against Online Threats: Helps keep your computer safe from viruses, ransomware, and other harmful attacks.
•	Keeping Settings Secure: Prevents accidental or unauthorized changes that could affect how your system works.
•	Reducing Mistakes and Misuse: Lowers the chance of downloading dangerous apps, sharing passwords, or misusing privileged access.
CyberArk Endpoint Privilege Manager (EPM) is already in place to provide administrative access to applications that require it.
________________________________________
Action Needed
No action is required from you.
If an application needs administrative access, CyberArk Endpoint Privilege Manager (EPM) will prompt you. If the prompt blocks the application from opening, you can request a review using the provided link within the CyberArk EPM message.






If you believe you need Local Administrator rights for your job duties, please contact The DOF IT Support team at [EMAIL_1] to have your request routed to an Information Security Officer (ISO).  Requests sent directly to the DTI Service Desk without ISO approval will be redirected to DOR’s ISOs.
